panels.title: CPU
panels.description: Busy percentage across all threads. Big number is the latest sample, the sparkline is the selected range. Legend under it: mean / max over the range.

panels.title: Memory
panels.description: RAM in use (total minus available) as a percentage.

panels.title: Temperature
panels.description: The hottest sensor on the box right now, named. Sensors the kernel gives no label fall back to their raw hwmon name.

targets.expr: topk(1, (label_replace(node_hwmon_temp_celsius{instance="homelab"} * on(instance,chip,sensor) group_left(label) node_hwmon_sensor_label{instance="homelab"}, "display", "$1", "label", "(.*)") or label_replace(node_hwmon_temp_celsius{instance="homelab"} unless on(instance,chip,sensor) node_hwmon_sensor_label{instance="homelab"}, "display", "$1", "chip", "(.*)")) * on(instance,chip) group_left(chip_name) node_hwmon_chip_names{instance="homelab"})

panels.title: Power
panels.description: Estimated wall power: APU package scaled for PSU loss plus the fixed platform offset.

panels.title: Network
panels.description: enp3s0 receive plus transmit, in bits per second.

panels.title: Wall power (estimated)
panels.description: APU package power scaled for PSU loss plus a fixed platform offset (NVMe, RAM, NIC, fan). See the recording rule in prometheus for the constants.

panels.title: APU package power
panels.description: Measured directly from the amdgpu PPT sensor. CPU + integrated GPU only.

panels.title: Energy per day
panels.description: 24h average wall power projected over a full day.

panels.title: Cost per month
panels.description: 30d projection at the cost_per_kwh dashboard variable.

panels.title: Memory
panels.description: `used` is total minus MemAvailable, so it excludes reclaimable page cache — this is the number to watch. `cache + buffers` is free RAM the kernel is borrowing for file cache and will hand back under pressure. `swap used` climbing while `used` stays low means vm.swappiness is evicting cold pages for no reason.

panels.title: Temperatures

targets.expr: max((label_replace(node_hwmon_temp_celsius{instance="homelab"} * on(instance,chip,sensor) group_left(label) node_hwmon_sensor_label{instance="homelab"}, "display", "$1", "label", "(.*)") or label_replace(node_hwmon_temp_celsius{instance="homelab"} unless on(instance,chip,sensor) node_hwmon_sensor_label{instance="homelab"}, "display", "$1", "chip", "(.*)")) * on(instance,chip) group_left(chip_name) node_hwmon_chip_names{instance="homelab"})

panels.description: Every hwmon sensor by its kernel label: Tctl is the CPU die, Composite / Sensor 1 / Sensor 2 are the NVMe, edge is the iGPU, spd5118 are the DIMMs. mt7921_phy0 is the WiFi chip on an interface that is DOWN, so it tracks case temperature rather than load. Sensors the kernel gives no label are named by their chip instead.

panels.title: Temperature min / avg / max (smoothed)
panels.description: Min, average and max across every sensor, smoothed over $smooth. The max line usually belongs to the WiFi chip or the NVMe rather than the CPU, and the WiFi interface is DOWN, so all three rising together means the case is heat-soaking, not that one component is working. The Temperatures panel above says which sensor is which.

panels.title: enp3s0 errors and drops
panels.description: Should stay flat at zero. A rising line means the NIC or the link is unhealthy.

panels.title: Container memory (RSS)
panels.description: Anonymous memory the container actually owns. Page cache is deliberately excluded: container_memory_working_set_bytes counts the kernel's file cache against the container, so an I/O-heavy container like qbittorrent reads as multiple GiB when its real footprint is a few MiB. That cache is reclaimable and is already shown on the host Memory panel.

panels.title: Who is watching
panels.description: One screen per active Jellyfin session on the NAS, drawn with three.js. The library is imported from a CDN at render time, so this panel needs the browser to reach jsdelivr.

panels.title: Transcoding
panels.description: Sessions the NAS is running ffmpeg for. Direct play costs it nothing; this is the number that shows up as CPU.

panels.title: Jellyfin API
panels.description: 0 also means the exporter has no API key: it reports the state rather than failing the scrape.
